scope_label: Conferral, conditioning and withdrawal of the status of authorised CBAM declarant (who may import goods)
pattern_rule: Status-conferral procedure: (application) -> (decision by the competent authority of the applicant's Member State) -> (registry entry and account set-up) -> (ongoing conditions: change reporting, guarantee) -> (revocation), the steps being tied by explicit legal cross-references.
governance_question: Who may import goods subject to the CBAM, and how is that status conferred, conditioned and withdrawn?
organizing_mechanism: Legally qualified coupling by explicit cross-references: A17(1) decides on applications 'submitted in accordance with Article 5'; A5(7) refers to the decision granting status 'pursuant to Article 17'; A16(3) sets up the account 'as soon as the authorisation referred to in Article 17(1) is granted'; A17(4) registers the decision in the CBAM registry; A17(8) revokes on grounds referring to Articles 22(1)-(2); A4 and A25(1) reserve importation to authorised CBAM declarants.
warrant_basis: The grouping is warranted by the stated procedural dependencies between application, decision, account and revocation, not by common chapter (Articles 4, 5, 16, 17 sit in Chapters II and III and Chapter V) or by the shared actor.
units_spanned: 45 distinct supporting units across: Chapter II (17 units); Chapter III (27 units); Chapter V (1 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: relations from the application (A5) to the closure of the account (A16(4)) and the status prohibitions (A4, A25(1)). Excluded: certificate sale (separate pattern), review and enforcement of declarant obligations (SC-05), operator registration (SC-02). Cross-part span: Articles 4, 5, 11, 16, 17, 25.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping 1: separate S for the application (A5) and for the decision (A17). Rival grouping 2: attach account administration (A16) to the registry (SC-02/SC-06) rather than to authorisation. The explicit trigger in A16(3) favours the present grouping but does not exclude the rivals.

scope_label: Registration of operators of third-country installations and disclosure of their verified information to authorised declarants
pattern_rule: Registration-on-request with deregistration and conditional disclosure: operator request -> Commission registration and notification -> operator verification duty -> operator-permitted disclosure -> declarant's permitted use.
governance_question: How are operators of third-country installations recorded in the CBAM registry and how may their verified emission information reach authorised CBAM declarants?
organizing_mechanism: Registration (A10(1)) makes the operator a registered operator to which A10(5)-(7) refer; A10(7) permits disclosure of the verification information to an authorised CBAM declarant; A8(2) lets the declarant use information disclosed 'in accordance with Article 10(7)' for installations 'registered in accordance with Article 10'; A14(3)-(4) governs the registry section and public access.
warrant_basis: Explicit cross-references between A10 and A8(2) link registration to the declarant's verification obligation; the grouping rests on this procedural dependency rather than on the shared actor (the Commission) or theme.
units_spanned: 12 distinct supporting units across: Chapter II (10 units); Chapter III (2 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: operator registration through deregistration, disclosure and public access. Excluded: verification duties (SC-03) and declarant obligations (SC-05). Cross-part span: Articles 8, 10, 14.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: attach the disclosure relations to the verification pattern (SC-03). The explicit reference to registration in A8(2) is why they are retained here.

scope_label: Accreditation of verifiers and verification of declared embedded emissions
pattern_rule: Accreditation-verification chain: national accreditation body accredits -> verifier verifies under the Annex VI principles -> authorised CBAM declarant (or operator) must ensure verification by an accredited verifier.
governance_question: How is the reliability of declared and operator-determined embedded emissions assured?
organizing_mechanism: A8(1) requires verification by 'a verifier accredited pursuant to Article 18' on the basis of the principles 'set out in Annex VI'; A18(2) accredits persons that can apply 'the verification principles referred to in Annex VI' for 'verification of the embedded emissions pursuant to Articles 8 and 10'; A10(5)(b) imposes the same on operators; Annex VI states the verifier's duties and report content.
warrant_basis: The grouping rests on explicit cross-references between A8, A10(5)(b), A18 and Annex VI; the Commission's implementing and delegated empowerments for verification are kept in SC-08.
units_spanned: 33 distinct supporting units across: Chapter II (6 units); Chapter III (2 units); Annex 4 (1 units); Annex 6 (24 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: accreditation, verification principles, report content and the declarant/operator duty to ensure verification. Cross-part span: Articles 8, 10, 18, Annexes IV and VI.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: split accreditation (A18) from verification duties (A8, Annex VI). Both are linked by the cross-reference to Annex VI in A18(2); the present grouping follows that link.

scope_label: Pricing, sale, repurchase and cancellation of CBAM certificates
pattern_rule: Certificate life-cycle on a Commission-run platform and registry: price calculation and publication -> sale by the Member State to declarants established there -> registry entry -> repurchase on request (cap) or cancellation (expiry), with suspension where a dispute is pending.
governance_question: How are CBAM certificates priced, issued to authorised declarants, repurchased or cancelled?
organizing_mechanism: A20(4) sells 'at the price calculated in accordance with Article 21'; A20(5) registers each sale in the declarant's account in the CBAM registry; A23(1) repurchases 'excess CBAM certificates remaining ... after the certificates have been surrendered in accordance with Article 22' through the platform 'referred to in Article 20'; A24 cancels certificates remaining in the registry account; A19(6) sends excess surrender to repurchase 'in accordance with Article 23'.
warrant_basis: Cross-references among A19(6), A20, A21, A22, A23 and A24 tie the steps; the grouping is not by chapter (Articles 19-24 span Chapters III and IV).
units_spanned: 16 distinct supporting units across: Chapter III (1 units); Chapter IV (15 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: price formation through repurchase and cancellation. Excluded: the surrender obligation itself (SC-05) and delegated acts on sale management (SC-08). Cross-part span: Articles 19-24.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: treat price formation (A21) separately from the sale/repurchase relations. A20(4) ties them.

scope_label: Declaration and surrender obligations of authorised declarants and their review, determination and sanction
pattern_rule: Escalation chain: declarant obligations (declare, calculate, keep records, surrender) -> Commission monitoring and review output (indicative) -> competent-authority determination and notification -> penalty imposition and recovery -> reporting back to the Commission.
governance_question: How are the declaration and surrender obligations of authorised CBAM declarants monitored, determined and sanctioned?
organizing_mechanism: A19(4) refers to failure to submit a declaration 'in accordance with Article 6'; A19(5) determines the number of certificates 'which should have been surrendered' and requests surrender; A22(3) leads from the Commission's finding on Article 22(2) to the competent authority's notification; A26(1)-(2) penalties follow failure to surrender (A22(1)) and are imposed by the competent authority under A26(4), 'including in light of the preliminary calculations made by the Commission in accordance with Article 19'; A17(8) cross-refers to infringements of A22(1)-(2).
warrant_basis: Explicit cross-references (A6, A19, A22, A26) and the stated hand-over between Commission input and the competent authority's definitive decision; not grouping by chapter (Articles 6, 7, 9, 15, 19, 22, 26, 31 span Chapters II, III, IV, VI, IX) or theme.
units_spanned: 78 distinct supporting units across: Chapter II (18 units); Chapter III (20 units); Chapter IV (6 units); Chapter V (1 units); Chapter VI (12 units); Chapter IX (1 units); Annex 4 (7 units); Annex 5 (13 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: obligations of the declarant from declaration to surrender and the control, determination and sanction relations that refer to them. Excluded: verification (SC-03), certificate market (SC-04), authorisation (SC-01) except the revocation relation (overlap). Cross-part span: Articles 6, 7, 9, 15, 17, 19, 22, 26, 31.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: split obligations (declaration and surrender) from the enforcement relations. The obligations are NAs without counterparties; the relations that refer to them are what give the set its relational warrant.

scope_label: Information transmission and secrecy among customs authorities, the Commission and competent authorities
pattern_rule: Information-interface chain in which the recipient of one transmission is the origin of the next (customs authorities -> Commission -> competent authority), bounded by a professional-secrecy rule with a stated sharing derogation.
governance_question: Which authorities transmit which information to which, and under what confidentiality?
organizing_mechanism: A25(3) has the Commission communicate 'the information referred to in paragraph 2' to the competent authority; A13(2) derogates from the secrecy of A13(1) for sharing 'such information' among competent authorities, the Commission, customs authorities, penalty authorities and the EPPO; A14(1) makes registry information available to customs authorities and competent authorities.
warrant_basis: The coupling is the explicit chaining of transmissions (A25(2) -> A25(3)) and the secrecy/derogation pair (A13(1)-(2)); the relations A11(1)-(2) and A12 are retained because A13(2) lets the same authorities share information 'with each other'.
units_spanned: 10 distinct supporting units across: Chapter III (7 units); Chapter V (3 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: information relations among customs authorities, the Commission and competent authorities and their secrecy limits. Cross-part span: Articles 11, 12, 13, 14, 25.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: separate the customs-data chain (A25) from the secrecy rule and from the authority-to-authority exchange (A11, A12). The grouping is the weakest of the set; A12 is typed with a nearest-fit relation type.

scope_label: Transitional reporting: information to importers, quarterly CBAM reports, correction and penalty
pattern_rule: Reporting-correction-penalty chain: customs authorities inform importers of the reporting obligation -> importer (or indirect customs representative) reports to the Commission -> Commission input to the competent authority -> competent authority corrects and penalises.
governance_question: How is the transitional-period reporting by importers collected, corrected and enforced?
organizing_mechanism: A33(1) informs importers of 'the reporting obligation referred to in Article 35'; A32 limits importer obligations to Articles 33-35; A35(3)-(5) link the Commission's list/information to the competent authority's correction procedure and penalty; A35(4) fixes the Commission's information as indicative.
warrant_basis: Explicit cross-references among Articles 32-35; not grouping by chapter alone (all in Chapter X) because the pattern is the information-correction-penalty sequence.
units_spanned: 28 distinct supporting units across: Chapter X (28 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: Articles 32-35 relations. Excluded: the definitive-period obligations (SC-05) and delegated acts (SC-08). Temporal limitation: the transitional period runs 1 October 2023 to 31 December 2025 (A32).
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: treat the transitional chain as an earlier phase of the SC-05 enforcement pattern. The obligation holders and the instruments differ, and A36(2) and A32 make the phases distinct in time.

scope_label: Conferral, control and procedure for the Commission's delegated and implementing acts
pattern_rule: Delegation-control pattern: conferral of delegated power by the European Parliament and the Council -> consultation of Member State experts -> notification -> objection or revocation; and assistance of the Commission by the CBAM Committee for implementing acts under the examination procedure.
governance_question: How is the Commission's secondary rule-making conferred and controlled?
organizing_mechanism: A28(2) names the empowering provisions (Articles 2(10), 2(11), 18(3), 20(6), 27(6)); A28(3)-(7) set revocation, consultation, notification and objection for delegated acts; each implementing-act empowerment refers to 'the examination procedure referred to in Article 29(2)', which A29(2) links to Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
warrant_basis: Explicit cross-references from each empowerment to A28 or A29; not grouping by theme (the empowerments sit in functional articles across Chapters I-IX).
units_spanned: 47 distinct supporting units across: Chapter I (1 units); Chapter II (12 units); Chapter III (10 units); Chapter IV (2 units); Chapter V (1 units); Chapter VI (1 units); Chapter VII (9 units); Chapter IX (1 units); Chapter X (7 units); Annex 4 (3 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: conferral, control and procedure for delegated and implementing acts; the empowerment assignments are included as members because they are the points at which the procedure is invoked. Cross-part span: Articles 2, 5-9, 14, 17, 18, 20, 21, 25, 27-29, 31, 35, Annex IV.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: split delegated acts (A28) and implementing acts (A29). The committee relation is dependent on an external Regulation, so the split is plausible; the present grouping follows the common function (Commission secondary rule-making).

scope_label: Listing and delisting of third countries and the conditional electricity exemption
pattern_rule: Conditional-exemption and listing pattern: conditions in A2(6)-(7) -> third-country reports and Commission assessment (A2(8)) -> removal conditions (A2(9)) -> delegated acts on requirements and list amendment (A2(10)-(11)), with an enabling Union competence for carbon-price agreements (A2(12)).
governance_question: How is the exclusion of third countries and territories from the scope of the Regulation, and the electricity exemption, conditioned and withdrawn?
organizing_mechanism: A2(7) conditions the exemption on 'the Commission has assessed ... in accordance with paragraph 8'; A2(8) requires two reports from the third country and Commission assessments; A2(9) removes a third country from the list on stated conditions; A2(10)-(11) empower the Commission to adopt delegated acts for removed countries and for list amendments by reference to paragraphs 6, 7 and 9.
warrant_basis: Explicit cross-references within Article 2(6)-(11); not grouping by chapter or theme.
units_spanned: 12 distinct supporting units across: Chapter I (8 units); Annex 3 (3 units); Annex 4 (1 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: Article 2(6)-(12), Annex III and the third-country demonstration in Annex IV point 4.3. Point 2 of Annex III is a placeholder, so no listed third country is evidenced.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: the list-amendment power (A2(11)) as part of the delegation pattern (SC-08) only. The conditions and the reporting/assessment relations are specific to this scope-management pattern.

scope_label: Notification and investigation of circumvention practices
pattern_rule: Notification-investigation pattern: eligible notifiers notify the Commission -> the Commission initiates and conducts an investigation, assisted by and notifying competent authorities.
governance_question: How are practices of circumvention of the Regulation notified and investigated?
organizing_mechanism: A27(4) allows notification; A27(5) makes the Commission initiate an investigation where it 'has been notified' by those parties and the notification meets the stated requirements, with assistance by and notification of competent authorities.
warrant_basis: Explicit cross-references within A27(4)-(5); the delegated-act power of A27(6) is not tied to the investigation outcome in the text.
units_spanned: 5 distinct supporting units across: Chapter VI (5 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: Article 27(3)-(6). The consequence of an investigation is not stated in W.
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: include the delegated-act power (A27(6)) as the consequence of the investigation. The text ties A27(6) to 'relevant data, reports and statistics', not to an investigation, so it is kept as an unlinked assignment.

scope_label: Commission reports and proposals to the European Parliament and the Council on the application of the Regulation
pattern_rule: Report-and-proposal pattern tied by explicit cross-reference: reports under A30(2)-(3), accompanied where appropriate by a legislative proposal under A30(4); information collected under A30(1) for the A30(2)(a) assessment.
governance_question: How does the Commission report to the legislators on scope extension and application before the end of the transitional period?
organizing_mechanism: A30(4) refers to 'the reports referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3'; A30(1) refers to 'paragraph 2, point (a)'.
warrant_basis: Only the relations linked by explicit cross-reference (A30(1), (2), (3), (4)) are grouped; the further reports of A30(5)-(8) share parties and theme only and are left as ungrouped relations (stop at R).
units_spanned: 16 distinct supporting units across: Chapter VIII (16 units) (full list in PROVENANCE_LINKS)
boundary_statement: Boundary: Article 30(1)-(4). Excluded: the periodic reports of A30(5)-(7) and the evaluation of A30(8).
competing_grouping: Rival grouping: all Article 30 reports as one S. Rejected as grouping by theme and recipients alone.
